9.meaning: the choice / the decision. Al-khiyara refers to the power or right of choice — the prerogative of selection. Here it emphasises that choosing belongs to Allah alone.

parts.en: the choice, the decision, the option (nominative)

9.grammar: Feminine noun in the nominative case (marfūʿ), -u (ḍamma) ending. Functions as the subject of a negated clause ('is not theirs').
9.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, preference; khiyara/khiyār: choice, option

10.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw, partner, or imperfection — 'Glory be! / How perfect He is!' It is a noun of glorification used to affirm absolute transcendence and purity.
10.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case, marked by the -a ending; it functions as an exclamation typically followed by a noun in the genitive ('Glory be to …'). It conveys the act of declaring someone free of any defect.
10.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; figuratively to declare free of imperfection

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'And He is exalted/transcendent high above' — to be far above and beyond, used of Allah being utterly lofty and removed from any deficiency or false attribution.
12.grammar: wa is 'and'. taʿālā is a past-tense verb (form VI) functioning as an exclamation of glorification; its final long -ā marks third-person masculine singular ('He'). The form intensifies the root sense to 'be supremely high, transcendent'.
12.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

13.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
13.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

14.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
14.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
14.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: 'And your Lord' — joins with 'and' the word rabb, the Master, Sustainer, Owner and Nurturer who creates, provides for and governs His servant, attached to a 'your' (one male).
1.grammar: Noun with 'and' in front and an attached possessor. The -u on rabb is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as a subject or as the thing being named/identified. The suffix -ka means 'your' for a single male.

2.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
2.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: conceals / hides. Refers to keeping something hidden within oneself — what the breast or chest keeps private and internal.

parts.en: it conceals, it hides, it keeps inward (Form IV, present 3rd feminine singular)

4.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person feminine singular (referring to 'the chests'), Form IV (akanna — to conceal). The ta- prefix marks 3rd feminine; -u is the indicative ending.
4.root: ك-ن-ن (k-n-n) — to conceal, to hide; Form IV: to keep hidden, to secrete

5.meaning: Breasts or chests — the inner being, the seat of feelings, intentions, and what a person keeps within; bosoms.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'breast/chest' (ṣadr). It is in the nominative (the -u before the pronoun), the case of the subject of a verb or sentence. The attached -hum is the possessive pronoun 'their' ('their breasts').
5.root: ص-د-ر (ṣ-d-r) — chest, front, the foremost part; the inner self

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: 'They make public / declare openly' — a present-tense verb meaning to announce, proclaim, or bring something into the open, the opposite of concealing it.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), in a causative-style form ('make open / announce'). The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are declaring.'
7.root: ع-ل-ن (ʿ-l-n) — openness; announcing, making public, declaring

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
4.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
4.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
6.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

7.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
7.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: The praise — all commendation, thanks, and laudation. With the article it conveys praise as a whole, in its entirety, belonging by right to the one praised.
8.grammar: A verbal noun with the definite article 'al-'. The '-u' ending is nominative, marking it as the subject/topic of a sentence; with the article it carries the sense of 'all praise' as an entire, comprehensive category.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: The first, the foremost, the initial one — the feminine form of the ordinal 'first', denoting that which comes before all others in order or time.
10.grammar: A definite ordinal adjective (with al-, 'the'), the feminine of 'first', so it describes a feminine noun. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case; it conveys priority in sequence ('the first/former').
10.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede, origin

11.meaning: And the Hereafter / and the next life: 'and' joined to 'the latter (abode)' — the life and final, lasting world that comes after this present one. From a root meaning 'last/later', it is the counterpart to this world (al-dunyā).
11.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the latter / the Hereafter') with conjunction 'wa-' ('and') and article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, the case used after prepositions or to link one noun to another ('… of …').
11.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; the end

12.meaning: 'And for Him / and to Him belongs' — the preposition 'for/to' expressing belonging or possession, joined with the pronoun 'Him.' It conveys that something belongs or is due to Him.
12.grammar: A small phrase: the connector 'and' plus the preposition la- ('for, to, belonging to') with the attached pronoun -hu ('Him'). The construction 'la- + pronoun' expresses possession or entitlement — 'and to Him belongs …' / 'and for Him is …'

13.meaning: 'The judgement / decision / authority to decide' — 'ḥukm' is a verdict, ruling, command or the very power and right to judge and decide matters. Made definite here as 'the decision/command'.
13.grammar: A definite noun with the '-u' ending, which marks the nominative case — typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'the decision is …'). 'al-' makes it 'the'.

14.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
14.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

15.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
15.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A rhetorical address meaning roughly 'Have you considered?' or 'Tell me — what do you think of…?'. It combines the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?') with the verb 'to see', here in the sense of mentally considering or reflecting on something rather than literal eyesight. It is addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying a subject built into its ending: the '-tum' ending marks a completed action done by 'you all' (masculine plural). Prefixed with the question particle 'a-', it turns the statement into a question, idiomatically 'have you considered / tell me'.
2.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, considering

3.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
3.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

4.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
5.root: — (proper divine name)

6.meaning: 'Upon / over you (plural)' — the preposition 'on, over, upon' with an attached 'you all' pronoun, indicating something coming onto or directed at a group.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -kum addresses a group ('you all'); the final -u (kumu) is a connecting helper-vowel easing the link into a following word that starts with the definite article. The preposition conveys 'on' or 'over'.

7.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
7.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
7.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

8.meaning: continuous / permanent / unending. Refers to something that goes on without cessation — perpetual, everlasting in its continuity.
8.grammar: Adverbial accusative (ẓarf), masculine indefinite, -an (tanwīn with fatḥa) ending.
8.root: س-ر-م-د (s-r-m-d) — continuous, perpetual, uninterrupted; sarmad: eternity, perpetuity

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
9.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

10.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
10.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').
10.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, period of time

11.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
11.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

12.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
12.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
12.root: — (pronoun)

13.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
13.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
13.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

14.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
14.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.
14.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, change

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'He/it brings (something) to you' or 'it comes to you' — the act of coming to, or bringing something to, a group of recipients. The single attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all') is the complement of the verb; the thing brought is not a separate pronoun within the word but is understood from context.
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb: the 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the attached '-kum' is the complement 'you all' (male/mixed group). The word contains only the subject prefix, the verb stem, and this '-kum' suffix — there is no separate 'it/him' object pronoun built in. So it conveys 'he/it comes to you' or 'he/it brings (it) to you'.

17.meaning: light / daylight. Ḍiyāʾ refers to brightness and radiance — the illumination that comes with daylight, enabling sight and activity.
17.grammar: Masculine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -in (kasra tanwīn) ending, after the preposition bi-.
17.root: ض-و-أ (ḍ-w-ʾ) — light, radiance; ḍiyāʾ: brilliance, illumination

18.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
18.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

19.meaning: You (plural) hear, listen, give ear. A present-tense verb from a root meaning 'to hear,' denoting the act of perceiving by ear, and by extension heeding or paying attention.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a plural masculine 'you all.' The full ending -ūna (with the final nūn intact) is the indicative mood, the default form used for plain factual statements ('you (all) hear').
19.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — to hear, to listen, to heed

7.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.

17.meaning: night. Al-layl refers to the night-time — the period of darkness that follows the day.
17.grammar: Masculine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -in (kasra tanwīn) ending, after the preposition bi-.
17.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night; layl: the night

18.meaning: (for) you (to) rest / so that you may rest. Refers to the purpose of the night — a time designed for rest and tranquillity.

parts.en: you rest, you find peace (Form I, present 2nd plural masculine)

18.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 2nd person masculine plural. The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; -ūna is the masculine plural indicative ending.
18.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to rest, to dwell; sukūn: stillness, rest

19.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
19.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

20.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
20.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

21.meaning: You (a group) see, perceive with the eyes, or look and discern — to take in something visually or grasp it with sight and insight. (The bare verb form means 'you see'; any negation comes from a separate particle.)
21.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb meaning 'to see/perceive'. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending supplies plurality, so the 't-' prefix together with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb is in its plain, unaltered present state.
21.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, to see and perceive

1.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
1.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

2.meaning: Mercy, compassion, tender care that actively benefits its object — joined to 'His': His mercy.
2.grammar: A feminine noun joined to the attached pronoun -hi ('his / its'). The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which appears because the noun is linked to a following possessor or follows a preposition ('... of ...'); the -hi suffix names that possessor: 'His mercy.' The original feminine -t- sound surfaces because a suffix follows.
2.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, loving care

3.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
3.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

4.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
4.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

5.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
5.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').
5.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, darkness

6.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
6.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.

7.meaning: So that you may find rest and stillness — to settle down, grow calm, and dwell at ease, the restlessness quieted into repose and tranquil dwelling.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb preceded by li- ('so that, in order to'), which expresses purpose and puts the verb in the subjunctive. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ū ending marks masculine plural ('you all') — note the subjunctive after li- drops the final -na.
7.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to rest, to dwell

8.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

9.meaning: 'And so that you may seek / desire' — to strive after and pursue something, to seek to obtain a benefit or bounty. The Form VIII verb conveys earnest seeking.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in Form VIII (to seek, desire) with 'and' plus the purpose-particle 'so that'. The ta- prefix means 'you'; the -ū ending (nūn dropped) marks plural 'you all' in the subjunctive of intent ('so that you may seek').
9.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
11.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
11.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

12.meaning: And so that you (plural) may; in the hope that you might. The particle laʿalla expresses hope, expectation, or a desired outcome ('perhaps / so that'), here with 'you' as its subject.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in the hope that

12.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps / in hope that'), which expresses an anticipated or hoped-for result, with the attached pronoun -kum ('you all') as its subject. Such particles place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -kum here is that subject. It typically leads into a verb stating the hoped outcome. The wa- ('and') links it to what comes before.

13.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: He will call them / He will summon them. Refers to the divine act of calling out to people on the Day of Judgement — addressing them with a question or announcement.

parts.en: He calls, He summons, He calls out to (Form III, present 3rd masculine singular)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

2.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person masculine singular, Form III (nādā — to call out to). The -ī is the stem ending of this hollow verb; -him is the plural object pronoun.
2.root: ن-د-و/ي (n-d-w/y) — to call; Form III: to call out to, to summon

3.meaning: Then/so He says — the verb 'say' joined to a connector meaning 'then' or 'so,' indicating a statement that follows as a consequence.
3.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb prefixed by 'then/so.' The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he.' The final -u ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of fact.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

4.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

5.meaning: My associates / partners — those alleged to share with someone in authority or divinity; shurakāʾ are co-sharers or partners, and with 'My' it denotes ones claimed as partners (e.g. falsely associated with Allah).
5.grammar: The plural of sharīk ('partner/associate') with the first-person possessive pronoun -iya ('my') attached. The -iya is the form the 'my' pronoun takes after this kind of plural ending; the whole means 'my partners/associates' — those claimed as co-sharers.
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, be a partner; hence associating partners (esp. with Allah)

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
7.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) claim / allege / assert' — to make a claim, often one that is unfounded or merely supposed. It frequently carries a tone of an unproven or false assertion.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all claim'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural indicative for a plain present statement.
8.root: ز-ع-م (z-ʿ-m) — to claim, allege, assert (often without proof)

1.meaning: And We removed / drew out / stripped away — to pull something out from where it was rooted or lodged, presented as a completed past action attributed to 'We'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural subject marker: it tells us the doer is 'we'. The past tense presents the action as already accomplished.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
2.root: — (preposition)

3.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
3.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
3.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

4.meaning: A community, nation, or people — a body of people bound together by shared faith, way of life, or origin; one collective group.
4.grammar: A feminine noun. The final -in (genitive with 'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a community') and links it to a preceding noun or preposition ('… of a community'). The feminine -t sound surfaces before the ending.

5.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
5.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.
5.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, testifying

6.meaning: 'So/then We said'. It combines a connector with the past-tense verb 'to say' done by 'we'.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed fa- ('so/then', showing sequence). The suffix -nā is the attached pronoun 'we', marking the subject of a completed act of speaking.

7.meaning: Bring (it) here!; produce it, hand it over, present it — a command directed at more than one person to bring forward or offer up something.
7.grammar: A plural command (imperative) addressed to a group of males or a mixed group: 'all of you, bring!' The -ū ending is the marker for a plural 'you' in a command. This is a defective verb of demand used only as an imperative meaning 'give/bring here.'

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'your proof / your evidence / your conclusive demonstration.' The base word denotes a decisive, clear-cut argument that establishes the truth of a claim beyond dispute, here possessed by a plural 'you.'
8.grammar: A noun carrying the -a accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or after certain particles. The attached -kum is a possessive pronoun meaning 'your,' addressing a group of males (or a mixed group), so the whole means 'your proof.'

9.meaning: Then they will know / So they shall learn. Refers to the moment of realisation on the Day of Judgement — the moment of belated understanding.

parts.en: they knew, they learned (past used for future certainty, 3rd plural)

9.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī) used with prophetic certainty for a future event, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the plural.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; ʿilm: knowledge

10.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
10.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

11.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
11.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
11.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

12.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
12.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

13.meaning: "And it went astray / was lost / went to ruin." A past-tense verb meaning that something strayed from the right path, missed its target, or vanished and came to nothing. The opening wa- adds "and."
13.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the "he/it" third-person masculine singular form. With no subject pronoun attached, the bare verb itself carries the sense "he/it strayed."
13.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be lost, err

14.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
14.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
14.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

15.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
15.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: They fabricate / invent (lies) — a third-person masculine plural present verb meaning to forge, concoct, or make up something falsely, typically a slander or a lie attributed to another.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern; the ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural, 'they.' The full ending -ūna (with its final -na intact) is the indicative, used for a real, ongoing, or habitual action ('they keep fabricating').
17.root: ف-ر-ي (f-r-y) — fabricating, forging, inventing falsely

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Qarun / Korah. Qārūn is the Quranic name for the man of immense wealth from the people of Moses — he became arrogant due to his riches and was swallowed by the earth.
2.grammar: Proper noun (diptote), taking the accusative/genitive marker -a (fatḥa) in both cases, as diptotes do not take kasra or tanwīn.

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: "people, folk, nation" — a community or tribe, especially a group bound together by kinship or shared belonging.
5.grammar: A collective noun (grammatically singular, referring to a group). The -i ending is the genitive case, typically linking the word to a following noun ("… OF …") or following a preposition.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group/community

6.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
6.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

7.meaning: but he oppressed / yet he wronged. Refers to someone going beyond what is just and acting tyrannically — transgressing against others.

parts.en: he oppressed, he transgressed, he was insolent (past, 3rd masculine singular)

7.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. The alif maqṣūra -ā is the stem ending.
7.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to transgress, to oppress, to be insolent; bughyān: tyranny

8.meaning: [on] them / over them. Refers to those upon whom injustice was done — the object of Qarun's oppression.
8.grammar: Preposition ʿalā ('upon, against') with the attached plural pronoun -him ('them'). A prepositional phrase indicating the object/direction.
8.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high; preposition ʿalā: upon, over, against

9.meaning: 'And We gave/granted him' — a verb of bestowing or handing over something, with 'We' as the giver and 'him' as the recipient. The root conveys the act of bringing or delivering a thing to someone so that they come to possess it.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The suffix -nā is the subject 'we' (the doers of the giving). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it' (the one given to). So the form packs subject and object into one word: 'we-gave-him'.
9.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: the treasures / the stored wealth. Al-kunūz refers to stockpiled treasure — accumulated hoards of gold, silver, and valuables.

parts.en: the treasures, the hoards (genitive broken plural)

11.grammar: Broken plural of kanz ('treasure, hoard'), genitive case (majrūr), -i (kasra) ending.
11.root: ك-ن-ز (k-n-z) — to hoard, to store up; kanz: treasure, hoard

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: (the) keys of it / its keys. Mafātiḥ refers to the keys used to open stored treasures — or figuratively the means of access to great wealth.
14.grammar: Broken plural of miftāḥ ('key'), in the accusative case (manṣūb), -a (fatḥa) ending (diptote, no tanwīn), in iḍāfa with -hu ('its').
14.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open; miftāḥ: key; mafātiḥ: keys

15.meaning: would burden / would weigh down. Refers to the weight being so great that a group of strong men would struggle to carry even the keys.

parts.en: it weighs down, it burdens, it is too heavy (Form I, present 3rd feminine singular)

15.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person feminine singular (referring to the keys). The emphatic lā precedes for strong assertion.
15.root: ن-و-أ (n-w-ʾ) — to weigh down, to burden; to be heavy

16.meaning: a company (of men) / a group of strong people. Refers to a band or party of physically strong individuals — a sizeable, able-bodied group.
16.grammar: Feminine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -ati ending, after the preposition bi-.
16.root: ع-ص-ب (ʿ-ṣ-b) — to bind together; ʿuṣba: a group, a band, a company

17.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
17.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

18.meaning: possessors of great strength / the mighty ones. Refers to people of exceptional physical power and might — here the strong men who struggle to carry the keys.
18.grammar: Feminine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -i (kasra) ending. It follows ūlū ('possessors of') which takes the genitive.
18.root: ق-و-و/ي (q-w-w/y) — strength, power; quwwa: force, might, power

19.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
19.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

20.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
20.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

21.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
21.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

22.meaning: 'his people / his folk' — the community, kinsfolk, or nation belonging to him.
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/community' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his') marking possession. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the noun as the subject — the one performing the action.

23.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
23.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

24.meaning: exult / rejoice arrogantly. An imperative (or jussive in a prohibition) referring to the act of revelling and exulting in pride — the exuberant, heedless joy of one drunk on worldly success.

parts.en: you exult, you rejoice (arrogantly), you revel (jussive/imperative, 2nd masculine singular)

24.grammar: Present-tense verb, jussive mood (majzūm), 2nd person masculine singular. Used after lā al-nāhiya ('do not'). The jussive drops the final -u.
24.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — to rejoice, to be happy; faraḥ: joy, exultation (sometimes with connotation of heedless pride)

25.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
25.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
26.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

27.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
27.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

28.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
28.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

29.meaning: the exultant / those who revel. Al-fariḥīn refers to those who are boastful and self-satisfied in their worldly pleasures — people who revel arrogantly in their gains.

parts.en: the exultant, those who revel arrogantly (masculine plural genitive/accusative)

29.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural, in the genitive/accusative case with -īna ending. Predicate or object complement.
29.root: ف-ر-ح (f-r-ḥ) — to rejoice; fariḥ: one who exults, one who revels

1.meaning: A phrase 'and seek' — joining the connector 'and' to a command to seek, pursue, desire, or strive after something. The verb conveys actively wanting and going after a goal.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a Form VIII command verb addressed to a second-person masculine singular ('you'). The trimmed final vowel (a weak-ending verb losing its last letter) marks it as an imperative — a direct instruction to 'seek'.
1.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after, pursue

2.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
2.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

3.meaning: Allah has given you / He has bestowed upon you. Refers to the gifts and blessings that Allah has granted — what has been given as provision.

parts.en: gave, bestowed (Form IV, past 3rd masculine singular)
you (2nd person masculine singular object pronoun)

3.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (ātā — to give, to bestow). -ka is the attached object pronoun ('you').
3.root: أ-ت-و/ي (ʾ-t-w/y) — to come; Form IV: to give, to bestow

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: the home / the Abode (of the Hereafter). Al-dār refers to a home or abode — here specifically al-dār al-ākhira, the Abode of the Hereafter, the final and ultimate dwelling.
5.grammar: Feminine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), -a (fatḥa) ending. Object of the preceding verb.
5.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to circle; dār: home, abode, dwelling

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
6.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
6.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: forget / neglect. Refers to the act of leaving something out of mind — forgetting or neglecting one's share of this world while pursuing the next.

parts.en: you forget, you neglect (jussive, 2nd masculine singular)

8.grammar: Present-tense verb, jussive mood (majzūm), 2nd person masculine singular. Used after lā al-nāhiya ('do not'). The jussive drops the -u ending.

9.meaning: your share / your portion. Naṣīb refers to one's allotted portion or lot — the share that is rightfully assigned to a person.
9.grammar: Masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), -a (fatḥa) ending, in iḍāfa with the possessive pronoun -ka ('your').
9.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up, to assign; naṣīb: one's allotted share or portion

10.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
10.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

12.meaning: And do good / And be generous. Refers to the act of performing good deeds and showing excellence and kindness to others.

parts.en: do good! be kind! be excellent! (masculine singular imperative, Form IV)

12.grammar: Masculine imperative, Form IV (aḥsana — to do good, to be excellent, to be kind). The -in ending is the jussive/imperative marker for Form IV.
12.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — good, beautiful; Form IV: to do good, to be kind, to excel

13.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
13.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
14.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.
14.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
16.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

17.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

18.meaning: seek / desire. Refers to pursuing or looking for something — here in the context of not seeking corruption in the land.

parts.en: you seek, you desire (jussive, 2nd masculine singular)

18.grammar: Present-tense verb, jussive mood (majzūm), 2nd person masculine singular. Used after lā al-nāhiya ('do not'). The jussive drops the -u and the hollow verb contracts.
18.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, to desire; also: to transgress, to cause corruption

19.meaning: Corruption, ruin, disorder, mischief — the state of things being spoiled or broken, the opposite of soundness and good order.

parts.en: corruption / ruin (the final -a is the accusative case ending, marking the direct object)

19.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-' = 'the') meaning 'corruption.' The final -a on 'fasāda' is the accusative case ending, which commonly marks the noun as a direct object ('… loves not corruption') or otherwise as something acted upon.
19.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoilage, disorder, the opposite of rightness

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
21.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

22.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
22.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

23.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
23.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
25.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

26.meaning: Those who spread corruption / the workers of mischief — people who ruin, disorder, and lay waste, the opposite of those who set things right.
26.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the.' An active participle (the one who corrupts) from the causative form (afʿala). The '-īna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition.
26.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — to be corrupt, spoil, cause ruin/disorder

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: I have been given it / I received it. Refers to something bestowed upon a person — here Qarun's claim that his wealth came from his own knowledge.

parts.en: I was given, I received (passive Form IV, past 1st singular)

3.grammar: Past-tense passive verb (māḍī majhūl), 1st person singular, Form IV. The -tu suffix marks 'I' as the subject; -hu is the attached object pronoun.
3.root: أ-ت-و/ي (ʾ-t-w/y) — to come; Form IV passive: to be given, to be bestowed upon

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
5.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'
5.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, certainty

6.meaning: 'With me / in my possession / in my keeping' — a word indicating presence, possession, or being at hand with the speaker. It points to what one has, holds, or holds as a view.

parts.en: at / with / in the possession of

6.grammar: An adverb of place/possession ('with, at, in the keeping of') joined to the possessive pronoun '-ī' ('me / my'). The base عِنۡدِ carries a short 'i' vowel (kasra) before the suffix, so the segment is read 'ʿindi'; with the attached '-ī' the whole word means 'with me / in my possession'.
6.root: — (adverb of place/possession; no triliteral verbal root)

7.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
7.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').
7.root: — (particles)

8.meaning: he know / he would know. Refers to the condition of being aware — here, referring to those who knew the truth about Qarun.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, jussive mood (majzūm), 3rd person masculine singular. Used in a conditional or purpose clause; the jussive drops the -u ending.

9.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
9.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
10.root: — (proper name)

11.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
11.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

12.meaning: Your family, your household and kinfolk — the people belonging to one's home and close circle, with 'your' attached.
12.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the word as an object or as the thing acted upon. The attached -ka means 'your' (one male), giving 'your family'.
12.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, household, people belonging to something

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: Before; the period or point in time (or place) prior to something. With the attached pronoun it means 'before it / before him', pointing to what came earlier.
14.grammar: An adverb/noun of time meaning 'before', functioning here as something governed in the genitive (the -i ending), as it regularly follows a preposition such as 'from'. The attached -hi means 'it / him' ('before it'); the vowel of the pronoun is -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows the -i ending.
14.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede; front, priorness

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: The generations — successive ages or peoples who lived and passed away one after another; a community of people belonging to a particular era.
16.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the generations'), with the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, marking the word as governed by something before it.
16.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — joining together; an age or generation

17.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
17.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
17.root: — (pronoun)

18.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
18.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

19.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
19.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
19.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

20.meaning: 'From it / out of it / from him'. It combines the preposition 'from / out of' with the pronoun 'it/him'.
20.grammar: The preposition min ('from / out of', indicating origin or source) with the attached pronoun -hu ('it' / 'him'), referring to a singular masculine thing or person. As object of the preposition, the pronoun is in the oblique form.
20.root: — (no triliteral root; a preposition with a pronoun)

21.meaning: Strength, power, force, might — physical or military vigour, robustness, and the capacity to exert force or prevail. Also used for firmness and resolve.
21.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the -an ending (the 'tanwīn' or 'n' of indefiniteness), so 'a strength / some power' with no 'the.' The accusative -an form is commonly used to specify in what respect something is meant ('in terms of strength') or as the object of a verb.
21.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, power

22.meaning: and greater / and more. Refers to something being more in quantity or degree — here describing how previous peoples were greater in wealth and numbers.

parts.en: more, greater in number, more abundant (comparative, nominative)

22.grammar: Comparative adjective (afʿal pattern), masculine, nominative case (marfūʿ), -u (ḍamma) ending. Used in a comparison.
22.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be many, to be abundant; aktharu: more, greater in number

23.meaning: 'A gathering / an assembling' — the verbal noun naming the act of bringing together, often used to intensify a related verb, conveying 'gathering them in one complete gathering'.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of gathering). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; on such a noun it commonly works as an emphasising 'inner object' — reinforcing a matching verb in the sense 'to gather a thorough gathering'.

24.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
24.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

25.meaning: He / it is asked / will be questioned — a person is questioned or called to account, with the questioner left unnamed (the passive 'is asked').
25.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive voice ('is/will be asked') and a third-person masculine singular subject — the one questioned — while the questioner is not named. The -u ending is the indicative mood, the marker of an actual or expected event.
25.root: س-ء-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, hold accountable

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

26.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

27.meaning: their sins / their offences. Refers to moral transgressions and offences — the wrongs committed by a group.

parts.en: sins, offences, transgressions (genitive broken plural construct)

27.grammar: Broken plural of dhanb ('sin, offence'), in the genitive case (majrūr), -i ending, in iḍāfa with -him (extended to -himu before vowel-initial words).
27.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, offence; dhanb: a fault, a transgression

28.meaning: The criminals, the guilty, the wrongdoers — those who deliberately commit grave sins and cut themselves off from what is right.
28.grammar: A noun (active participle, 'one who commits crime/sin') with the definite article al-, in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative — the form used when such people are the subject/doer, marking 'the ones who…' as the actors.
28.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin, guilt

1.meaning: 'Then he came out / went forth' — the past-tense verb 'to go out, emerge, depart,' marked for a single male subject, opening with 'then/so' to mark sequence.
