1.grammar: A past-tense verb with a third-person singular masculine subject built in ('he'). The final '-a' is the standard past-tense vowel for this form, not a case marker. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then/so' and signals that this follows on from what came before.
1.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: 'His people / his folk' — the community, tribe, or nation to which a person belongs, with the attached pronoun 'his'.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this genitive '-i'.
3.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: his adornment / his finery. Refers to the splendid display of wealth and beautiful things — Qarun's ostentatious show of riches.
5.grammar: Feminine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -ati ending, in iḍāfa with the possessive pronoun -hi ('his').
5.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — beauty, adornment; zīna: decoration, ornamentation

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
8.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

9.meaning: "the life" — the state of being alive; living existence, vitality.
9.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -a ending (on the feminine -t) is accusative, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb or the noun governed by certain particles.
9.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live, life

10.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
10.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
10.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

11.meaning: A wistful exclamation of longing — 'Oh, would that…!' or 'If only…!' — combining a vocative cry of yearning with a particle that wishes for something hoped-for but typically out of reach.
11.grammar: A compound exclamation. The particle layta expresses a wish or yearning for something unlikely or impossible, like English 'if only'. The prefixed yā- here is not calling a person but intensifies the cry of longing. Layta normally governs a following noun in the accusative as the thing wished for.

12.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
12.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

13.meaning: The like of / similar to; a match, equivalent, or counterpart — 'the same as' or 'something resembling.'
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'the like of.' The -a ending is the accusative case, the form typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — so it points to 'the like (of something)' as what is involved in the action.

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'was given / was granted / was brought (something)'. It conveys that someone received something from an unnamed giver, with the focus on the recipient and the gift rather than the giver.

parts.en: was (passive prefix of the Form IV verb 'to give/bring')
given/brought (middle root letter of the passive stem)
final weak root letter (yāʾ) surfacing in the passive perfect

15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the passive voice, third person masculine singular ('he/it was given'). It is the passive of a Form IV verb (active 'to give/bring'), formed from the Form IV stem rather than by a Form I internal vowel change; the subject ending is zero (no added pronoun). The final -ya is the weak third root letter (yāʾ) appearing in this passive perfect form, not a personal suffix.
15.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring or give

16.meaning: (to) Qarun. Qarun in the dative/accusative — the person being addressed or referred to in the relevant clause.
16.grammar: Proper noun (diptote), nominative case (marfūʿ), -u (ḍamma) ending. Used here as the subject of a clause.

17.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
17.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

18.meaning: An emphatic statement that someone is truly the holder or owner of something. The opening lām is a particle of emphasis ('surely/indeed'), and dhū means 'owner of, possessor of, the one endowed with' — it is a word that always governs a following noun to say someone is rich in or characterized by that thing.
18.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that strengthens a statement ('indeed, surely'). Dhū is one of the special 'five nouns'; its long -ū ending marks the nominative (subject) case, the form used when this word is the doer or the thing being described, and it must be followed by a noun in the genitive ('possessor OF …').

19.meaning: (of) fortune / of luck. Ḥaẓẓ refers to one's assigned fortune, luck, or portion — what fate or divine will has allotted to a person.
19.grammar: Masculine noun in the genitive case (majrūr), -in (kasra tanwīn with geminated ẓāʾ) ending.
19.root: ح-ظ-ظ (ḥ-ẓ-ẓ) — fortune, luck, one's allotted share

20.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
20.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
20.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
3.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
3.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

4.meaning: Knowledge — sure, established awareness and understanding of how things truly are, as opposed to ignorance, guesswork, or mere opinion.
4.grammar: A definite noun ('the knowledge'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing being received or acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case.
4.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, sure awareness

5.meaning: "woe to you" — an exclamation of warning, threat, or distress directed at a group; it announces ruin, calamity, or a severe rebuke coming upon the addressees.
5.grammar: An exclamatory noun "wayl" (woe/ruin) fixed in the accusative with -a, joined to -kum ("you," plural). It works as a set cry of warning or distress aimed at several people; the accusative reflects its use as an exclamation of woe befalling them.
5.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — woe, ruin, doom (an outcry of calamity)

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'reward,' 'recompense,' or 'requital' — the return or repayment given for one's deeds. The root conveys returning something or giving back in kind.
6.grammar: A noun ('reward'). The final -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (the 'doer' or the topic), as opposed to an object.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
8.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
8.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

9.meaning: A combined expression meaning 'to whom?' or 'for whom?' — it asks about the owner or the one to whom something belongs. It fuses the preposition 'to/for' with the question word 'who'.
9.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the interrogative 'who'. Together they pose the question 'to whom (does it belong)?'. The combination is fixed in form and does not change its ending.

10.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.
10.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, faith

11.meaning: "And he did / worked / acted" — to do or perform an action, to put work into effect. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he did'. The bare -a ending with no attached pronoun marks this completed, masculine 'he' action. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work / do / act

12.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
12.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
12.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: it is granted / it is given. Refers to something being bestowed or conferred upon someone — a quality that is given, not self-acquired.

parts.en: it is granted, it is given (passive Form II, present 3rd masculine singular)

14.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (mudāriʿ majhūl), 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (laqqā — to cause to meet; passive: to be given). -hā is the feminine object pronoun.
14.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet; Form II passive: to be given, to be granted

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: (to) the patient ones / those who persevere. Al-ṣābirūn refers to those who exercise ṣabr — the quality of patient endurance through hardship, restraint, and steadfast perseverance.

parts.en: the patient ones, those who persevere (masculine plural nominative)

16.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural, Form I, nominative case (marfūʿ), indicated by -ūna.
16.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — patience, endurance; ṣabr: patient perseverance

1.meaning: Then We caused to swallow up / So We made (the earth) engulf. Refers to the divine punishment upon Qarun — the earth swallowing him.

parts.en: we caused to sink in, we made (the earth) engulf (past, 1st plural)

1.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 1st person plural, Form I (khasafa — to sink in, to engulf; when transitive: to cause the earth to swallow). The -nā suffix marks 'we'.
1.root: خ-س-ف (kh-s-f) — to sink in, to engulf; khasf: the earth swallowing/sinking

2.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

3.meaning: and his home / and his house. Refers to Qarun's dwelling — the residence that was also swallowed up by the earth.

parts.en: and the home/abode of (preposition + noun, genitive construct)

3.grammar: Feminine noun dār ('home, abode') in the genitive case (majrūr) after the preposition bi-, in iḍāfa with the possessive pronoun -hi ('his').
3.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to circle; dār: home, abode

4.meaning: the earth / the ground. Al-arḍ refers to the earth itself — the ground, the land, the physical earth.
4.grammar: Feminine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), -a (fatḥa) ending. Object of the preceding verb.
4.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, ground, land; arḍ: the earth

5.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
5.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

6.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

6.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A group, band, or company of people — a detachment or faction, especially a body of fighters. It denotes a portion of a larger whole that has banded together.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun, here indefinite (no 'the'). The ending '-in' (the tā' marbūṭa pronounced with nunation, '-tin') is the indefinite genitive: it marks the noun as 'a group' linked to/governed by a preceding word, such as a counting particle or preposition.
9.root: ف-أ-ي (f-ʾ-y) — to split off; a faction/group

10.meaning: They help / support / give victory to him; a verb of coming to someone's aid against an enemy, with 'him' as the one helped — joining the ideas of assistance and triumph.
10.grammar: A Form I imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), with the attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The ya- prefix with the -ū- plural marker forms the masculine plural subject; the retained -na is the indicative (marfūʿ) ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('they help / are helping').
10.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to grant victory

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
11.root: — (preposition)

12.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
12.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
12.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic, 'Allah' — the unique, sole Deity worthy of worship.
13.grammar: The divine proper name. The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to a preceding noun in a possessive sense ('… of Allah'). As a proper name it is inherently definite and takes no indefinite 'n' sound.

14.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
14.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
14.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

15.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

15.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

16.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

17.meaning: those who (could) defend themselves / helpers. Al-muntaṣirīn refers to those who can resist or retaliate — people with the power to help themselves or others.

parts.en: those who defend themselves, those who can retaliate (masculine plural genitive/accusative)

17.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil), Form VIII (intaṣara — to defend oneself, to gain a victory), masculine plural, genitive/accusative case with -īna ending.
17.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — help, victory; Form VIII: to help oneself, to gain a victory, to resist

1.meaning: And became / And turned out to be. The verb aṣbaḥa ('to enter the morning') is used in Arabic to mean 'came to be (in a state)' — describing the onset or emergence of a new condition.

parts.en: became, came to be in a state (literally 'entered morning')

1.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (afʿala). The -a ending marks the past tense.
1.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning; Form IV: to become, to come to be

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: (had) wished / had longed. Refers to the act of wishing or desiring something — here those who had envied Qarun now wish they had not envied him.

parts.en: they wished, they longed for, they desired (Form V, past 3rd plural)

3.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine plural, Form V (tamnna — to wish, to long for). The -aw ending marks the plural past.
3.root: م-ن-ي (m-n-y) — to wish, to desire; Form V: to wish for, to long for

4.meaning: 'Its place' or 'its location' — the spot or position belonging to it.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('its / his'). The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb or an adverb of place ('in its place').

5.meaning: 'Yesterday / in the recent past' — the day before today; idiomatically, a time just gone by.
5.grammar: The noun 'yesterday' with the prefixed preposition bi- ('in/on') and the definite article al-. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition (here 'on the yesterday' = 'yesterday').
5.root: أ-م-س (ʾ-m-s) — yesterday, the recent past

6.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

7.meaning: Ah! That / Oh! As if. Wayka-anna is a Quranic expression of astonished realisation — it means something like 'Indeed! (We now see that)…' or 'Oh, as if we didn't know that…'

parts.en: Ah! Indeed! Oh, to think that… (exclamation of astonished realisation)

7.grammar: A compound expression: way (exclamation of grief/surprise) + ka (as, like) + anna (that). Functions as an exclamation introducing a realised truth.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: He spreads out, extends, stretches forth, and makes ample. The verb conveys laying something open and wide, and so giving abundantly or enlarging a provision.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; the 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he extends / keeps extending'). The root pictures spreading a thing out flat and wide, hence giving generously.
9.root: ب-س-ط (b-s-ṭ) — spreading out, extending, expanding, making ample

10.meaning: The provision; sustenance, livelihood, and the means of life — whatever bounty is granted to support and nourish a creature, whether food, wealth, or any good thing bestowed.
10.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the'; its 'r' doubles the sun-letter assimilation of the 'l'). It is a verbal noun on the 'fiʿl' pattern denoting that which is provided. The final '-a' is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing given or acted upon).
10.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowing the means of life

11.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
11.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

12.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
12.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'His servants / His slaves / His worshippers' — ʿibād are those who serve and worship; with the attached pronoun it denotes the servants belonging to Him (Allah), i.e., humankind or His devotees.
14.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel is the genitive case, typically appearing after a preposition or in a possessive ('of') link; the pronoun names the one to whom the servants belong.
14.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — serving, worshipping, devoted obedience

15.meaning: And He measures out, restricts, straitens, or apportions sparingly; to set a fixed measure to provision so as to limit it. The same verb can also mean to have power and to determine.
15.grammar: The prefix 'wa' means 'and'. The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; 'ya-' marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' marks the plain indicative — an ongoing or habitual action ('he restricts / keeps measuring out'). The root joins the ideas of measuring, decreeing, and having power.

16.meaning: A particle of urging or exhortation meaning 'why not …?' — used to press for or demand that something be done, and sometimes to express a wish, often with a tone of reproach ('why does … not happen?').
16.grammar: An indivisible particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). Although written as one form, it is not built up from the conditional 'if' plus a negation; in this prompting usage it is a single fixed particle meaning 'why not?' / 'if only.' Followed by a verb it presses for that action. (Note: in a different construction the same form can mean 'were it not for,' but that is a separate usage.) It is a particle and takes no case ending.

17.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
17.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
17.root: — (particle; no root)

18.meaning: Allah had favoured / (He) had shown grace. Refers to the divine act of granting special favour and blessing — the recognition that Allah's grace was withheld from Qarun.

parts.en: He bestowed favour, He showed grace (Form I, past 3rd masculine singular)

18.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (manna — to bestow favour). The doubled nūn is the Form I doubling.
18.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow favour, to confer a blessing; manna: grace, bestowed favour

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
19.root: — (proper divine name)

20.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
20.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

21.meaning: He would have caused it to swallow us / He would have made it engulf us. Refers to the hypothetical situation — had Allah not shown favour, the earth would have swallowed the onlookers too.

parts.en: surely (emphatic lām of the apodosis in a conditional)
He would have engulfed (past used in hypothetical condition)

21.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī) used in a hypothetical conditional apodosis, 3rd person masculine singular. The emphatic lā marks the beginning of the result clause.
21.root: خ-س-ف (kh-s-f) — to sink in, to engulf; khasf: swallowing/sinking into the earth

22.meaning: A particle 'with/for/by' joined to the word 'us'. It signals accompaniment, means, or that something concerns or befalls 'us'.
22.grammar: The preposition bi- always attaches to the front of a noun or pronoun and puts it in the genitive. Here it is fused with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'), the first-person plural object. The bi- can convey 'with', 'by means of', or that an event happens 'to/concerning' the people named.

23.meaning: Ah! That he / Oh, as if he. A variant of the exclamation wayka-anna in id 838 — here with the attached masculine singular pronoun -hu ('he').

parts.en: Ah! Indeed! Oh, to think that…
he (pronoun subject of the following clause)

23.grammar: Compound exclamation (way + ka + anna) + attached pronoun -hu introducing the content of the astonished realisation.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'he succeeds / prospers / attains salvation' — to thrive and reach what is sought while escaping what is feared; ultimate well-being and triumph, including success in the Hereafter.
25.grammar: Present-tense verb (form IV), third-person masculine singular ('he succeeds'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending for a plain present statement.
25.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to prosper, succeed, attain, be saved

26.meaning: The disbelievers, ingrates, or those who reject faith; people who cover over and refuse the truth. The root sense is to conceal or be ungrateful, so it denotes both denial of faith and ingratitude.
26.grammar: A definite masculine plural noun (an active participle) with the article al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the 'nominative' state, which generally identifies the doer or subject of a sentence.
26.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, be ungrateful

1.meaning: That; a demonstrative used to point to something distant or already mentioned. It singles out a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing, roughly 'that one over there.'
1.grammar: A feminine singular demonstrative pronoun pointing to something far off. The -ka element signals remoteness ('that yonder' rather than 'this near'). Being a demonstrative, it does not take case endings; its form is fixed.

2.meaning: A noun meaning 'the home / the abode / the dwelling-place' — a settled place of residence or a realm in which one abides.
2.grammar: A definite noun, made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking the noun as the subject or the thing being identified. So it reads 'the home/abode'.
2.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — turning, circling; dwelling

3.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the last (one) / the final', referring to what comes last and to the life to come after this world.
3.grammar: A definite feminine adjective made definite by al- ('the'). The feminine ending is written with tāʾ marbūṭa (ة); before a following case vowel it is pronounced as -t-, so the suffix here sounds -atu: the -a- is the feminine marker and the -u is the nominative case (the case used for the subject or the thing being identified, or to match a noun in that role). It conveys 'the last / the final (one)'.
3.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

4.meaning: We assign it / We grant it. Refers to the divine act of designating or giving the abode of the Hereafter to a specific group of people.

parts.en: we make, we assign, we grant (Form I, present 1st plural)

4.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 1st person plural, Form I. The na- prefix marks 'we'; -u is the indicative ending. -hā is the attached feminine object pronoun.
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to assign, to appoint

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
5.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
7.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.
7.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend

8.meaning: Loftiness, exaltation — being high or elevated; when applied to conduct it means arrogance, overbearing pride, or tyrannical superiority.
8.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act/state' noun) of rising high. The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking the word as an object or as an adverbial/specifying complement.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
10.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
10.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'corruption, mischief, ruin' — the spoiling of right order, moral or social wrongdoing and disorder in the land. Here in the form that often answers 'doing what?' — i.e. spreading corruption.
12.grammar: A masculine verbal noun ('corruption, mischief'). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative: the -a marks the accusative case (often expressing the aim, manner, or object of an action — 'spreading corruption'), and the final -n ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite.
12.root: ف-س-د (f-s-d) — corruption, spoiling, decay, disorder

13.meaning: 'And the final outcome / the end result'; the noun for what comes last — the ultimate consequence or destiny that follows after a course of events.
13.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -u ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence. With 'and' it reads 'and the final outcome'.
13.root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b) — to follow, come after; an end/consequence

14.meaning: For the people of taqwā — the God-conscious, those who are mindful and careful of Allah, guarding themselves against wrongdoing out of awareness of Him. The whole word means 'for/to the God-conscious ones'.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

14.grammar: An active participle in the sound masculine plural, prefixed by the preposition 'li-' ('for/to') and the definite article 'al-'. The '-īna' ending is the oblique (genitive/accusative) plural form, used after a preposition; it means 'the (several) ones who…'. The base verb form (Form VIII) carries a reflexive sense: those who shield or protect themselves.
14.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield; hence taqwā: God-conscious caution

1.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
1.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive

3.meaning: 'With / for the good deed' — the noun ḥasana (a good deed, a fine thing, a benefit) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It denotes a beautiful or beneficial act or reward.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, which is required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built into the word.
3.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

4.meaning: So for him / then his is; a linking word 'so/then' joined to 'for him,' expressing that something belongs or accrues to a single male — 'so to him belongs…'
4.grammar: A cluster of particles: the connector fa- ('so, then, and as a result') + the preposition la- ('for, belonging to') + the pronoun -hu ('him'). Together they assign possession or entitlement to a single male: 'so for him (is)…'

5.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
5.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
5.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

6.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
6.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.

7.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
7.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
7.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

9.meaning: 'With / for the evil deed' — the noun sayyi'a (a bad deed, an evil or harmful thing) made definite ('the') and governed by the preposition bi- ('with/for/by'). It is the counterpart of the 'good deed.'
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with/for') and the article (written al- but pronounced as-sayyi'a because the s is a 'sun letter' that absorbs the l). The final -i marks the genitive case, required after a preposition. The feminine -a(t) ending is built in.
9.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, harm

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
10.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

11.meaning: will be recompensed / will receive his reward. Refers to receiving what one deserves — the ultimate payment of reward or punishment proportional to one's deeds.

parts.en: he is recompensed, he receives his reward/punishment (passive Form I, present 3rd masculine singular)

11.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (mudāriʿ majhūl), 3rd person masculine singular. The alif maqṣūra -ā is the passive stem ending. The -y (alif maqṣūra) marks the passive of hollow/defective verb roots.
11.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to reward, to repay, to recompense; jazāʾ: recompense, reward

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
13.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

14.meaning: 'The evil deeds / bad actions' — plural of sayyi'a, a wrong or evil act, a misdeed or sin; the opposite of a good deed.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the misdeeds'). The -i ending here is the case marker for the sound feminine plural in the genitive/accusative state, typically signalling that it follows a preposition, links to a preceding noun, or stands as an object.
14.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; misdeed, wrong

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
18.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
18.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb whose core sense is 'to make obligatory, impose as a duty, ordain'; it also carries the related senses 'to appoint/allot a fixed share' and 'to undertake / bind oneself to a duty'. As shown, it means 'he made obligatory / he ordained'.
3.grammar: A completed (past) action in the basic faʿala pattern for a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/one [did it]'). There is no separable subject suffix on this form: the final fatḥa (-a) sitting on the last root letter is part of the verb stem itself, not an added ending, and the doer 'he' is understood from the pattern alone. A separate pronoun-suffix would appear only for other subjects (for example -tu 'I', -ta/-ti 'you', -tum 'you all').
3.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — making obligatory; ordaining a fixed duty or share

4.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
4.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

5.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
5.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
5.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

6.meaning: (will) surely take you back / will certainly return you. Refers to the divine promise of returning the Prophet to Mecca — a promise of homecoming and ultimate victory.

parts.en: the one who returns, the one who brings back (active participle, construct)
you (2nd person masculine singular object pronoun)

6.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) of Form I (radda — to return, to bring back), masculine singular, in the construct state with the object pronoun -ka ('you'). The emphatic lā precedes for strong assertion.
6.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, to send back; radd: return, restoration

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: a place of return / a destination. Maʿād refers to the place or time of return — the final destination, often referring to the Hereafter as the ultimate return point, but here also understood as Mecca.

parts.en: a place of return, a destination, a point of return (genitive indefinite)

8.grammar: Masculine noun (verbal noun/place noun, faʿāl pattern from ʿāda 'to return'), in the genitive case (majrūr), indicated by -in (kasra tanwīn).
8.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return; maʿād: the place/time of return

9.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

10.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
10.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.
10.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining

11.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
11.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

12.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
12.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
12.root: — (pronoun)

13.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

14.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'with/through the guidance'. It combines the preposition 'with/by means of' and the noun hudā — right guidance, the clear showing of the correct way and being led upon it.
14.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the definite noun al-hudā ('the guidance'). Because hudā ends in a fixed long vowel (a 'frozen' ending), its case does not visibly change after the preposition, though it stands in the genitive that bi- requires.
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

15.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
15.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

16.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
16.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
17.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
17.root: — (particle)

18.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
18.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
18.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

19.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
19.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
19.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

3.meaning: expecting / hoping for. Refers to the act of hoping or anticipating something — here, the Prophet not expecting the revelation before it came to him.

parts.en: you hope for, you expect, you anticipate (present, 2nd masculine singular)

3.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 2nd person masculine singular, Form I. The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū is the hollow verb stem ending. Final alif is a spelling convention.
3.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — to hope for, to expect, to anticipate

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: would be sent down / would be revealed. Refers to revelation being cast down from above — the sending down of the Quran.

parts.en: it is cast, it is sent down, it is revealed (passive Form IV, present 3rd masculine singular)

5.grammar: Present-tense passive verb (mudāriʿ majhūl), 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (ulqiya — to be cast, to be revealed). The alif maqṣūra -ā marks the passive.
5.root: ل-ق-و/ي (l-q-w/y) — to throw, to cast; Form IV: to cast down, to send down (revelation)

6.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
6.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

7.meaning: 'The Book / Scripture / what is prescribed in writing' — a written record or ordinance; the decreed, written prescription. Often denotes revealed Scripture or, by extension, a fixed written decree.
7.grammar: A verbal noun on the fiʿāl pattern ('that which is written') with the definite article al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
7.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write / prescribe / ordain

8.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
8.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

9.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.
9.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
11.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery, sustaining

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
12.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

13.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
13.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

14.meaning: A helper, supporter, or backer; one who lends aid and strengthens another. The form can also carry a collective sense, 'helpers/backers acting in support'.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, meaning a steadfast supporter (literally one who 'backs up'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a helper'), commonly marking the object of a verb or a predicate/state-describing word.
14.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, to support/back up, to appear

15.meaning: to the disbelievers / for the unbelievers. Refers to those who reject the faith — the people who refuse to acknowledge the truth.

parts.en: for the, to the (preposition + definite article)
the disbelievers, the rejecters (masculine plural genitive)

15.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural, genitive case (majrūr) after the preposition lā, with -īna ending.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, to disbelieve; kāfir: one who disbelieves, a rejecter

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: avert you / turn you away. Refers to the act of diverting someone from the right course — here, the fear that the disbelievers will try to turn the Prophet away from the revelations.

parts.en: they will surely avert you, they will turn you away (Form I present + nūn of strong emphasis)

2.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person masculine plural, with the emphatic nūn of strong assertion (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla) — the doubled -nn- indicates strong emphasis. -ka is the object pronoun.
2.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to avert, to turn away, to prevent; ṣadd: turning away, deterrence

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

4.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
4.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
6.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

8.meaning: It (feminine) was sent down / revealed — a completed act in which something (such as a passage of scripture) was brought down from on high, with a feminine subject.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the 'afʿala' pattern ('was caused to come down / was revealed'). The internal vowel pattern (u–i) marks it as passive ('was …-ed' rather than 'did'). The '-at' ending marks a feminine singular subject: 'it (fem.) was sent down.'
8.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come/send down, descend, reveal

9.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
9.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.
9.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

10.meaning: And invite (people) / And call (to Allah). Refers to the act of dāʿwa — inviting people to the path of Allah and proclaiming the message.

parts.en: invite! call! summon! (masculine singular imperative, Form I)

10.grammar: Masculine imperative, Form I (daʿā — to call, to invite). The imperative of hollow verbs uses a shortened form with connecting alif.
10.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite; daʿwa: a call, an invitation

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
11.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

12.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
12.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

13.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

14.meaning: You must certainly be / never be — an emphatic form of the verb 'to be', stressing that one truly will (or, with a negative, truly must not) be in a certain state.
14.grammar: A present-tense form of the verb 'to be', addressed to 'you' (the prefix ta-). The heavy ending -anna (nūn of emphasis) gives a strong, insistent force — 'you most certainly are/must be' — and is the standard way Arabic stresses a command or warning attached to a verb.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

15.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
15.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

16.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
16.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: You call upon, invoke, pray to, or summon. The verb daʿā covers calling out to someone, appealing to them for help, and supplication.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person-masculine-singular subject ('you'). Built on a root whose last letter is weak: in the plain indicative this verb ends in a long -ū (tadʿū), but here the weak letter has dropped away, leaving the bare short -u of the shortened (jussive) form — the shape this verb takes after certain particles or in conditional clauses.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invoke, supplicate

3.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
3.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
5.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
5.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

6.meaning: Another, other, a different one — a further item distinct from the one already mentioned.
6.grammar: An adjective/noun meaning 'other'. It belongs to a small group of words that resist the usual indefinite -n (nunation), so even when indefinite it takes a plain -a ending. That final -a is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or one in agreement with such a noun.
6.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after, other

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
8.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
8.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
9.root: — (particle)

10.meaning: Him. Huwa is the 3rd person masculine singular independent pronoun — referring to Allah. Used for emphasis or as a subject pronoun.

parts.en: He (3rd person masculine singular independent pronoun)

10.grammar: Independent personal pronoun, 3rd person masculine singular. Used for emphasis or as the subject of a clause, referring to Allah.

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
