11.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.
11.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, wholeness, comprehensiveness

12.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

13.meaning: (will be) destroyed / will perish. Hālik refers to something or someone that will inevitably perish and come to an end — utterly destroyed.

parts.en: perishing, (will be) destroyed, doomed (active participle, nominative)

13.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine singular, nominative case (marfūʿ), indicated by -un (tanwīn with ḍamma). Functions as a predicate ('everything is perishing/will perish').
13.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, to be destroyed; halāk: destruction, perdition

14.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
14.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
14.root: — (particle)

15.meaning: His face; the front of the head — and by extension one's whole self, presence, or the direction in which one turns. 'Surrendering one's face' idiomatically means devoting one's entire being.
15.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu meaning 'his.' The -a on the stem is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). With the pronoun it means 'his face/self.'
15.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, aspect; what one turns toward

16.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
16.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
16.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: 'The judgement / decision / authority to decide' — 'ḥukm' is a verdict, ruling, command or the very power and right to judge and decide matters. Made definite here as 'the decision/command'.
17.grammar: A definite noun with the '-u' ending, which marks the nominative case — typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'the decision is …'). 'al-' makes it 'the'.
17.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — judging, governing, wisdom

18.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
18.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (all) are brought back / returned' — to be made to go back to a point of origin. The passive voice frames the subjects as acted upon, not acting.
19.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) passive verb, Form I. In the passive the vowel pattern (tu-…-a-) shows the subject is being acted upon: 'you are returned' rather than 'you return'. The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks masculine plural ('you all') and indicative mood (a real, ongoing or certain event). Together: 'you all are brought back / returned'.
19.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, bring back
